ai.literal: Distress coming-time let-laugh; it (acc.) having-approached overcoming that equaling is-not.
ai.translation: When adversity comes, laugh. To confront and overcome it, there is nothing equal to that.
ai.modern: துன்பம் வரும்போது அதனைப் பார்த்துச் சிரிக்கவும். அந்தத் துன்பத்தை எதிர்த்து வெல்வதற்கு அந்தச் சிரிப்பை விடச் சிறந்தது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises a counter-intuitive response to trouble: laughter. The word 'இடுக்கண்' means distress or adversity. When it arrives, one should laugh or smile ('நகுக'). To confront and ride over that distress ('அடுத்து ஊர்வது'), there is nothing equal to that cheerful, unshrinking attitude. Laughter here signifies courage and a clear mind, which are the best tools to overcome difficulties.

ai.literal: Of-flood like sorrow wisdom-possessor by-mind to-think will-perish.
ai.translation: Sorrow that seems as vast as a flood will vanish the moment a wise man sizes it up in his mind.
ai.modern: வெள்ளம் போலப் பெருகி வரும் துன்பமும், அறிவுடையவன் தன் உள்ளத்தால் அதன் தன்மையை நினைத்த அளவிலேயே அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates how a wise person handles overwhelming difficulties. Trouble may appear as vast and unstoppable as a flood. However, a person equipped with wisdom does not panic. The moment he calmly evaluates the situation in his mind, the seemingly insurmountable sorrow loses its power and perishes. The contrast between the massive physical flood and the simple mental act of thinking highlights the supreme power of a clear mind over external adversity.

ai.literal: To sorrow sorrow they will inflict, to sorrow sorrow those who do not suffer.
ai.translation: Those who do not suffer sorrow when facing sorrow will inflict sorrow upon sorrow itself.
ai.modern: துன்பம் வந்த போது அதற்காகத் துன்பப்படாதவர்கள், அந்தத் துன்பத்திற்கே துன்பத்தை உண்டாக்குவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet plays on the word 'இடும்பை' (sorrow or affliction) to emphasize mental resilience. When trouble arrives, an ordinary person feels sorrow. However, those who refuse to be troubled by trouble turn the tables on adversity. By remaining unbroken, they effectively inflict suffering upon suffering itself, defeating it completely.

ai.literal: Obstructed place all draught-bull like-he experienced trouble distress it-has.
ai.translation: The trouble that comes to a man who pulls like a draught bull through every obstructed path will itself suffer distress.
ai.modern: தடைகள் நிறைந்த இடங்களிலெல்லாம் வண்டியை இழுத்துச் செல்லும் எருதினைப் போலத் தளராமல் உழைப்பவனுக்கு வரும் துன்பமே, அவனது உறுதியைக் கண்டு துன்பப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the image of a strong draught bull ('பகடு') pulling a cart steadily through steep and obstructed terrain ('மடுத்த வாய் எல்லாம்'). A person who shows the same relentless strength and perseverance when facing obstacles will overcome them. The poet playfully states that the trouble ('இடுக்கண்') afflicting such a person will itself experience distress ('இடர்ப்பாடு உடைத்து') and be defeated by his unyielding spirit.

ai.literal: Piling up even if (they) come, despair he-who-has-not experienced trouble, trouble will suffer.
ai.translation: The trouble experienced by a man who does not despair even when hardships come piling up, will itself suffer trouble.
ai.modern: துன்பங்கள் ஒன்றன்பின் ஒன்றாக அடுக்கிக்கொண்டு வந்தாலும் மனம் தளராதவன் அடைந்த துன்பமே, அவனிடம் தோற்றுத் துன்பப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet personifies trouble to illustrate the power of a resilient mind. It states that if a person refuses to despair even when hardships come one after another, the hardship itself will suffer. The word 'அழிவு' (destruction) here refers to the breaking down or despair of the mind. By standing firm, the resilient person turns the tables, making 'இடுக்கண்' (trouble) experience 'இடுக்கண்' (trouble) and ultimately defeating it.

ai.literal: "We are destitute" saying, sorrow will they suffer? "We have obtained" saying, cherishing those who do not know.
ai.translation: Will those who do not cherish wealth saying "we have gained it", suffer sorrow in poverty saying "we are destitute"?
ai.modern: 'செல்வத்தைப் பெற்றோம்' என்று மகிழ்ந்து அதைக் கொண்டாடத் தெரியாதவர்கள், வறுமை வந்தபோது 'எல்லாம் இழந்தோம்' என்று கூறித் துன்பப்படுவார்களா? மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the mindset of the wise who remain balanced in both prosperity and adversity. The word 'பெற்றேம்' (we have gained) refers to acquiring wealth, while 'அற்றேம்' (we are destitute) refers to losing it. The author asks a rhetorical question: if a person does not overly cherish or celebrate their gains, will they suffer sorrow when they lose them? By treating both gain and loss with the same equanimity, one avoids despair during difficult times.

ai.literal: Target body to suffering knowing that, trouble as helplessness will not consider indeed the great.
ai.translation: Knowing that the body is a natural target for suffering, great people will not consider trouble as a state of helplessness.
ai.modern: உடம்பு துன்பத்திற்கு ஓர் இலக்கு என்பதை உணர்ந்து, சிறந்த மனிதர்கள் தமக்கு வரும் துன்பத்தைக் கண்டு கலங்கிச் செயலற்றுப் போக மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the mindset of great people when facing adversity. They understand that the physical body is naturally a target for pain and suffering. Because they accept this fundamental truth, they do not view sudden troubles as a source of helpless confusion. Instead, they remain steadfast and unfaltering in the face of hardship.

ai.literal: Pleasure he-desires-not affliction nature he-who-says sorrow experiencing he-is-without.
ai.translation: He who does not crave pleasure and considers affliction to be natural will not experience sorrow.
ai.modern: இன்பத்தை விரும்பாதவனாய், துன்பம் வருவது இயற்கையே என்று கருதுபவன், வாழ்வில் துன்பத்தை அடைய மாட்டான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to remain unaffected by hardships. It states that a person who does not actively chase after pleasure and accepts that difficulties are a natural part of life will not feel the sting of sorrow. The word 'விழையான்' shows detachment from seeking joy, while 'இயல்பு என்பான்' shows a realistic acceptance of trouble. By balancing these two attitudes, the mind becomes immune to suffering.

ai.literal: In pleasure pleasure he who does not desire, in sorrow sorrow experiencing he is without.
ai.translation: He who does not crave pleasure in times of joy will not suffer sorrow in times of trouble.
ai.modern: இன்பம் வரும் காலத்தில் அதனை விரும்பி மயங்காதவன், துன்பம் வரும் காலத்தில் அதற்காக வருந்த மாட்டான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet teaches the importance of emotional equanimity. The word 'விழையாதான்' describes a person who does not actively crave or cling to joy when circumstances are favorable. Because this person does not attach themselves to fleeting happiness, they do not experience 'துன்பம்' (sorrow) as a crushing burden when facing difficulties. The parallel structure emphasizes that maintaining balance during good times is the very foundation of resilience during bad times.

ai.literal: Suffering joy as if one takes, will come to be one's foes desiring greatness.
ai.translation: If one embraces adversity as joy, one will attain a greatness that even one's enemies admire.
ai.modern: துன்பத்தையே இன்பமாக ஏற்றுக்கொண்டால், ஒருவனுக்கு அவனுடைய பகைவரும் விரும்பும் பெருமை உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet teaches the mindset needed to overcome adversity. By choosing to view suffering ('இன்னாமை') as a form of joy ('இன்பம்'), a person demonstrates extraordinary resilience. Such an unshakable attitude elevates their character to a level of greatness ('சிறப்பு') that commands respect and admiration even from their enemies ('ஒன்னார்'). The word 'விழையும்' highlights that this greatness is so compelling that foes themselves wish they possessed it.
